title: HC Mike LaFleur Postgame Press Conference | Week 11 vs. Kansas City Chiefs
headline: Carson Beck is day to day with back spasms and stayed home; Cody Simon (calf) gets an MRI Monday; Harrison Wallace III is emerging as a bright spot.
summary: LaFleur said Arizona's offense scored only seven points against Kansas City on the road, and he put the blame on himself first and on the team as a collective. He said Carson Beck was kept home to get treatment for back spasms and called him day to day, with no timetable. A different quarterback, called "Josh" in the captions, played this week after taking no reps Wednesday or Thursday, and LaFleur praised his competitiveness. He noted that four different quarterbacks in four weeks has made cadences and procedures inconsistent, but said he did not want it to sound like an excuse. He defended the aggressive fourth-down decision but said there was a better play to call. He called Harrison Wallace III a bright spot who is not overwhelmed by the moment, and he cited several of his recent catches. LaFleur declined to explain why Max Melton was fully benched and said it would stay in-house, though he praised Melton's return-game work. He said he needs to rewatch the offensive line tape, that the run game did not get going until late, and that the offense did not call enough runs. He also said Cody Simon (calf) did not return and will have an MRI.

injuries.detail: Left the game with a calf injury and did not return; MRI scheduled for Monday.
Back spasms; stayed home from the trip for treatment and is day to day with no timetable.

signals.claim: Wallace will keep building his role and the offense will continue to showcase him.
signals.note: He is trending up in the passing game, with a slot fade, a quick out on third down and a flat route all praised, which makes him a watch-list WR add.
signals.quote: he's definitely been a bright spot for us

signals.claim: Melton was fully benched on defense this week after rotating previously, but he contributed in the return game.
signals.note: His defensive role is unclear and the coach would not explain the benching, though he still has return value.
signals.quote: he helped us tremendously today in the return game

signals.claim: Beck's availability is day to day with back spasms and there is no set return date.
signals.note: His status is uncertain, so check the injury report before setting lineups that depend on Arizona's QB.
signals.quote: there's no magic pill you can take for that

signals.claim: Simon will have an MRI on his calf on Monday.
signals.note: He is the only player who did not return from the game; IDP managers should wait on the MRI result.
signals.quote: he had a calf, and we'll MRI it tomorrow

topics.detail: Arizona has used four different quarterbacks in four weeks, and a QB called "Josh" in the captions started this game; he is not on the provided roster, so he is not named. LaFleur said the constant change affects cadences and procedures, and that if Beck is down again, the QB would at least get a full week of practice with the first team.

LaFleur said he would make the aggressive fourth-down decision again, noting the team had to be aggressive against this opponent and quarterback. He disliked the play call and wished execution and clarity had been better.

The run game did not get going until the end and LaFleur said the offense did not call enough runs. He liked the second-to-last drive until a holding penalty knocked the offense back, and he said he needs to watch the film before judging the line.

Kansas City held the offense to 118 rushing yards, but the run defense gave up early gashes before settling in. LaFleur said the defense needs to rush with four and cover better against pressure-beating plans.

Six games remain, five of them at home, and LaFleur said he held a blunt postgame talk with the team. He brought injured-reserve players on the trip to see what a championship-caliber standard looks like.

title: Jesse Minter Recaps Ravens’ Week 11 Loss to Panthers
headline: Derrick Henry's status is unknown after the 35-33 loss to Carolina, and LaJohntay Wester's punt-return job is under review.
summary: Minter credited Carolina for a back-and-forth game. He said the first half was chaotic because of turnovers, and that Baltimore never got going in the third quarter, when it turned the ball over and failed to hold the ball. The Ravens had the lead late and could not hold it, and Minter took responsibility for that. He said he called the defense that allowed the go-ahead score and wished he had put his players in better spots on two third downs. On the final drive he said he considered taking the penalty and also burning a timeout, and in hindsight he could have called a timeout to calm things down. Asked about Derrick Henry, he said only that there was no update. He said the team will have to look at its punt-return situation after several mistakes there. He called the team's effort strong over the last two weeks but said it keeps failing to finish games, and he told the team to get back to work.

injuries.detail: Asked for an update after the game, Minter said only 'No update.' He gave no diagnosis and no outlook for next week.

signals.note: The coach gave no information on Henry's health, so his availability next week is unknown. Monitor the injury report and consider a handcuff such as Justice Hill.
signals.quote: No update.

signals.claim: Wester's role as punt returner will be reviewed and could change after repeated mistakes.
signals.note: Wester could lose punt-return work, which matters in leagues that count return yards, though his offensive role was not discussed.
signals.quote: we'll definitely have to look at that.

topics.detail: Minter said he considered taking the penalty and a timeout on the final drive. He chose field position and wanted to keep a good pass rusher on the field, but he conceded a timeout would have helped.
Minter said he calls the defensive plays and took blame for the go-ahead drive, citing two third-down situations he wishes he had handled better.
Turnovers, including a fumble return, and a lack of rhythm in the third quarter swung the game. Baltimore got a safety early and led late but did not close it out, and its losing streak continues.

title: Joe Brady Talks Cleaning Things Up After Divisional Win Against The Miami Dolphins
headline: Bills beat Miami 26-9 and Joe Brady praised James Cook, Khalil Shakir and DJ Moore. Dalton Kincaid was out, DJ Moore left briefly in the first half and returned, and Brady plans to run more and pass less on a short week.
summary: Joe Brady was frustrated despite the 26-9 win. He said the 45 dropbacks were too many for a game Buffalo led and blamed his own play-calling. He praised James Cook for his improved ball security and said Cook is playing as well as anyone in the league, though he wanted to run the ball more. Khalil Shakir got heavy praise for his run blocking and slot work, with the offense in a lot of 11 personnel and Dalton Kincaid out. Brady called DJ Moore tough, a big reason Buffalo traded for him, and said he is still being integrated, with Brady sometimes needing to manage his playing time. Moore left briefly in the first half and returned, and Brady will check with the medical staff. Gregory Rousseau was praised for his length and confidence as he reaches a career-high ten sacks. Brady cited penalties, field goals instead of touchdowns, and a quiet offensive line and run game as clean-up items before Thursday's Thanksgiving game. He also said he hopes to get Christian Benford back, and he described a defensive rotation in which Maxwell Hairston and Jalon Kilgore got work. A fake punt and a flea flicker were part of his aim to show different ways to win.

injuries.detail: Banged up briefly in the first half, then returned. Brady will go over it with the medical staff after the press conference.
Was listed doubtful with a thumb injury and did not play. Brady was asked at the end if he was close to playing, but the answer is not in the transcript.
Brady said he hopes to get Benford back, which implies he missed this game. No timeline was given.

signals.claim: Cook's ball security has improved, and Buffalo wants to run the ball more when leading.
signals.note: Brady called Cook elite and said the run game was underused, so Cook is a strong volume play if Buffalo leads again.
signals.quote: Jimbo's playing as good as anybody in the NFL right now.

signals.claim: Shakir stays a key slot and 11-personnel piece, especially with Kincaid out.
signals.note: Brady lauded Shakir's unselfishness and production, and the offense leaned on 11 personnel without Kincaid.
signals.quote: anytime we can get Khalil on the field, we're a better football team.

signals.claim: Moore will get more comfortable in the system as he plays full games, and can be moved around the formation.
signals.note: Brady sees Moore as a dynamic, versatile piece whose role should grow, though a first-half injury scare needs watching.
signals.quote: he makes us so much better and he makes plays

signals.claim: Buffalo should not throw 45 times in a game it is leading, so pass volume should come down in similar game scripts.
signals.note: Brady owned the heavy dropback count as a play-calling mistake, so passing volume may drop when Buffalo leads.
signals.quote: I don't think we should ever be throwing the ball 45 times.

signals.claim: Rousseau keeps winning one-on-one matchups on the edge against tackles.
signals.note: He is at a career-high ten sacks, and Brady credits his length and confidence, so he is a strong IDP edge option.
signals.quote: he's had a career high with ten sacks.

signals.claim: Hairston is in the defensive rotation while Benford is out.
signals.note: Brady called the rotation good and hopes to get Benford back, so Hairston's workload could shrink if Benford returns.

topics.detail: Brady listed pre-snap penalties on offense and defense, special teams penalties, and too many field goals as problems. He said repeated mistakes cannot continue.
Asked about the line's struggles and the lack of push in the run game, Brady said he wasn't good enough and needs to watch the tape.
Buffalo tried to get a look for an onside kick, did not get it, and took a delay. The fake punt worked, with Brady saying it was repped a lot in practice. He wants to show multiple ways to win.

Brady praised the defense's pre-snap communication and execution. He highlighted Trey White's return (questionable before the game, cleared after a morning workout) and Jalon Kilgore getting more opportunity.
Buffalo plays again on Thursday (Thanksgiving). Brady said the team focused only on this game, did not call it differently because of the short week, and will regroup immediately.

title: Dave Canales: 'This is how we play football'
headline: Jalen Coker is in concussion protocol after the 35-33 win over the Ravens, so his availability next week is uncertain. Bryce Young got praise for his final-drive poise, and Trevor Etienne is working in as a change-of-pace back behind a heavily used Chuba Hubbard.
summary: Canales praised Carolina's fight through seven lead changes in the 35-33 win over Baltimore. He singled out Will Lee's return, which included two forced fumbles (one at the goal line) and a tipped pass that became the game-sealing interception. The coach said the offense had balance, with the run game going and explosives evening out in the second half. He still wants touchdowns instead of field goals in the red zone and more of a killer instinct. Jalen Coker is in concussion protocol and will be evaluated again tomorrow. The coach gave no further update. Bryce Young drew praise for his rhythm, his first and second-read completions and his control on the last drive. Canales also described a competitive streak that showed after a flag. Canales said Tetairoa McMillan and Coker made tough catches in traffic. He said Princely Umanmielen was clear-headed, emotionally steady and got a sack on a stunt. He said Chuba Hubbard's workload is heavy because of how hard he runs, so Trevor Etienne is giving the offense fresh legs and keeps improving. Canales also called out a special-teams returner (the name was garbled in the captions) for needing to secure the ball and not get cute with kicks near the goal line. Penalties were down from recent weeks, and he said the team is two games clear in the NFC South.

injuries.detail: In concussion protocol. The team will keep evaluating him tomorrow, and Canales had nothing more beyond that.
Played in the game after spending some time off, and Canales called it an amazing comeback.

signals.claim: Coker remains in concussion protocol and will be re-evaluated tomorrow, with no timeline given.
signals.note: Coker's availability next week is uncertain, so check the injury report before setting lineups.
signals.quote: they're still going to evaluate him. So tomorrow will be the continual evaluation there.

signals.claim: Carolina has a trick play with Coker taking the snap and pitching to Bryce Young. It had been in the works for two to three weeks and was used in this game.
signals.note: Gadget usage shows Coker is involved in the game plan, but it is a low-volume play.

signals.claim: McMillan remains a featured target who wins in tight windows and in traffic.
signals.note: Canales had wanted more from the receivers after last week, and this game gave positive reinforcement for McMillan's role.
signals.quote: the guys made some incredible catches in traffic, getting hit, finishing those plays

signals.claim: Young is trusted to run the offense in late-game situations. He found explosives and completions off his first and second reads, and Canales wants better red-zone finishing.
signals.note: The coach's confidence in Young is high, but red-zone scoring is still a stated area for improvement.
signals.quote: He's going to be focused and locked into the moment.

signals.claim: Hubbard is carrying a heavy volume and Canales is monitoring him live, working in a change-of-pace back for rest.
signals.note: Hubbard is still the lead back, but his workload is being watched, and the rest snaps go to Etienne.
signals.quote: it's good to have fresh legs to come in there

signals.claim: Etienne will keep getting opportunities on offense and special teams as he continues to improve.
signals.note: He is a handcuff and change-of-pace option who is earning more trust from the coaching staff.
signals.quote: each time he gets an opportunity on offense, he just keeps getting better and better

signals.claim: Umanmielen is growing in emotional control and in impact as a pass rusher.
signals.note: He had a sack on a stunt, so he is a rising defensive piece for IDP formats.
signals.quote: a very clear headed young player looking for his opportunities

signals.claim: Lee returned from time off with two forced fumbles and a tipped pass that became the game-sealing interception.
signals.note: Lee made major plays on defense, which matters for IDP and the defense's overall outlook.
signals.quote: you never give up as long as you've got a blade of grass

topics.detail: Canales wants the offense to turn red-zone chances and turnovers into touchdowns and show more killer instinct to run away with games.
Penalties were significantly down from recent weeks, with cleaner pre-snap play. A couple of unnecessary-roughness flags after plays remained.

The defense had tackling issues early, including a long Derrick Henry run, but settled in and closed out the game. Baltimore's Jacoby Brissett distributed well, with Zay Flowers involved and Henry and Justice Hill as the run game.
A returner (the name was garbled in the captions) had three chances for a big play and needs to secure the ball. Canales said not to get cute with kicks that land near the goal line.
Carolina is two games clear in the NFC South. Canales had challenged the team early in the week to play its best football with a chance to create distance.

title: Ben Johnson on Bears' 21-13 win over Saints | Press Conference
headline: Roschon Johnson is the only injury of note (ankle) heading into a short week, and the Bears' run game stayed under 4 yards per carry in the 21-13 win over New Orleans.
summary: Ben Johnson was happy to open the second half of the season 1-0 after the bye. He gave most of the credit to a defense that played hard for 60 minutes, piling up sacks and turnovers that became points. The offense turned those short fields into touchdowns, and the fourth-quarter safety was another big moment. The one concern was the ground game: the runners finished under four yards a carry and missed the efficiency target that was a point of emphasis coming off the bye. The only injury he mentioned was an ankle for Roschon Johnson, whose status will be clearer as the week goes on. Jeffery Simmons got a game ball and is quickly becoming a vocal leader the team rallies behind. Johnson also praised a young receiver (not clearly named in the captions) as an elite-speed playmaker whose package of plays will keep growing as he earns more trust. He called the Thursday divisional road game a quick turnaround and said the team is focused only on getting ready for it.

injuries.detail: Johnson called him the one injury of note, with an ankle; the team will see how it turns out through the week on a short turnaround before Thursday.

injuries.player: Unnamed young WR (Luther Burden III or Zavion Thomas)
injuries.detail: A question about a young speedster's role and last week's benching was never tied to a name in the captions. Burden (concussion, full practice) and Thomas (ankle, questionable) both fit, so it is unclear who was meant and no signal is attributed.

signals.claim: Ankle injury will be monitored through the week, with availability for Thursday's game uncertain.
signals.note: He is the only injury Johnson flagged, so his Thursday availability is worth tracking on a short week.
signals.quote: He's got an ankle, so we'll see how that turns out

signals.claim: Simmons will keep growing as a leader and voice in the locker room as he gets to know teammates.
signals.note: He earned a game ball and is making explosive plays, which supports his role as a defensive centerpiece.
signals.quote: Becoming a voice that everyone hears and everyone rallies behind.

topics.detail: Chicago's runners averaged under four yards a carry, missing the efficiency target that was a point of emphasis after the bye. Johnson said the staff will study why.

The defense had six sacks and several turnovers that became points. Johnson said that having built leads in recent weeks has made opponents one-dimensional, and that the pass rush is best when it forces second-and-long and third downs.
Johnson called him dangerous and still improving, noting his five fourth-quarter comebacks and his ability to extend plays with his legs.
A quick Thursday divisional road game follows. Johnson called it worth 'one and a half' games and said the focus is purely on preparing for it.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: Postgame Week 11 #TENvsDAL
headline: Dallas' 51-30 win over Tennessee scored on all eight drives with Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens all producing. Javonte Williams and James Houston saw bigger roles, and there's a quick turnaround to Philadelphia.
summary: Schottenheimer was very proud of the defense, which responded after a tough week and a play-calling change (Mike Patton's first game calling plays). He said the unit simplified the menu, tackled and communicated better, and executed well, with only the penalty to start the second half hurting. The offense scored on all eight drives, and he called Dak Prescott incredible. He praised the line and depth guys such as James Mitchell and T.J. Bass, and said six different players scored. He said the team tries to run most things through Lamb and Pickens, who both topped 100 yards, but stressed it was a complete team effort. Javonte Williams got going in the run game, with outside zone working, and stood out in blitz pickup and on checkdowns. Jashaun Corbin, the RB2 candidate, ran hard and made a good pickup on a Pickens play. James Houston played more, and Schottenheimer praised his pass-rush moves. Injury news was minor: Dee Winters has a knee contusion and Cobie Durant cleared concussion protocol. The focus now turns immediately to Philadelphia on a short week.

injuries.detail: Has a knee contusion; coach said he 'came out pretty good' and gave no timeline.
Cleared concussion protocol already and could have returned to the game, but the staff chose not to put him back in.
A reporter referenced him being hurt as a big loss at RB2; the coach gave no update on him.

signals.note: Led an offense that scored on all eight drives and added a rushing TD, with the coach saying he throws to the first open man.
signals.quote: I thought he was incredible.

signals.claim: Lamb will remain a primary focus of the passing offense.
signals.note: Coach says the offense runs most things through Lamb and Pickens, which supports their weekly volume.
signals.quote: we try to run most things through them

signals.claim: Pickens will remain a primary focus of the passing offense.
signals.note: Coach says the offense runs most things through Lamb and Pickens, which supports their weekly volume.
signals.quote: we try to run most things through them

signals.claim: Williams will keep a significant role on early downs, as a pass protector and on checkdowns.
signals.note: His blitz pickup and receiving work, plus the run game getting going, point to a role that holds him on the field.
signals.quote: Javonte Williams was incredible just in blitz pickup

signals.claim: Houston will keep getting more defensive playing time as a pass rusher.
signals.note: Confirmed he played more and was used in different personnel, which is relevant for IDP sack upside.
signals.quote: we know what James is capable of

signals.note: Singled out for strong play with Jake Ferguson out, which could matter if the TE room stays thin.
signals.quote: James Mitchell doesn't get talked about enough.

topics.detail: Mike Patton called plays for the first time, working alongside Christian Parker. The menu was tighter, with a focus on doing simple things better, tackling, and takeaways. The defense got a fumble recovery and a plus-one turnover margin.
Jashaun Corbin (not on the provided roster) ran hard and was praised as the RB2 candidate, with Goodson injured. He was also credited with a pickup on a Pickens play.
Coach said the team has to get into the tournament, and is not looking beyond the next opponent. Dallas is 5-6 after this win.
Dallas plays Philadelphia again in a couple of days and the staff will start on film right away.

title: Campbell on Week 11 performance
headline: Goff was the catalyst in a Week 11 win over Tampa Bay, and the Lions are on a short week with a Thursday Thanksgiving game; Campbell also praised the defensive line.
summary: Campbell was proud of the team after beating a Tampa Bay defense he called one of the league's best, and said the Lions have been improving for about four weeks. The plan was to put the ball in Jared Goff's hands early, let the skill players work, and find the run game as the game went on. He called Goff the catalyst and praised how he handles the heavy weekly load of audibles, kills and protections. He also praised Goff's pocket movement and escapes. The run game was tough for three quarters before it opened up late. Campbell credited a young offensive line that is growing, with Juice Scruggs still new at center. He called the defense the biggest area of growth, saying it has kept getting better despite losing some critical players. He named Alim McNeill, Tyleik Williams and Tyler Lacy as disruptive up front, and said the line responded after last week's loss. He noted they did not get a turnover but did get a punch-out. The Lions now turn to a Thursday Thanksgiving game, where they will open the day's slate.

signals.claim: The offense will keep leaning on Goff and the passing game when the plan calls for it, as it did early against Tampa.
signals.note: Campbell said the plan was to put the ball in Goff's hands early, and he credited Goff with handling a huge weekly game plan, which supports his QB1 outlook.
signals.quote: he was really our catalyst today.

signals.claim: The staff is working to find the best runs and creases for Gibbs, and the run game can open up late in games.
signals.note: The run game was tough for three quarters before it broke open in the fourth, so Gibbs's production can depend on game flow.
signals.quote: Find some crease for for Gibbs.

signals.claim: Scruggs is the starting center and is still adjusting to the position.
signals.note: A young offensive line with a new center is improving, which affects the run game and Goff's protection.
signals.quote: he's new to us at center. But he's getting better.

signals.note: Campbell singled McNeill out as disruptive inside, which helps his IDP value.
signals.quote: Mack I thought was, you know, disruptive in there.

signals.note: Williams made a lot of plays again, so he is a rising IDP piece on the defensive line.
signals.quote: Ty Leake again made a lot of plays.

signals.note: Lacy made an early impact on a play-action pass, and his strength pushing the pocket is a plus for the pass rush.
signals.quote: he can push the pocket.

topics.detail: Campbell called the line youthful but growing fast. Scruggs is new at center, and Mahogany, Ratledge and Miller are gaining strength. They protected Goff well and came off the ball.
Tampa had the league's top run defense. Detroit kept pounding the run through three tough quarters and it opened up in the fourth for big gains to seal the game.

Campbell called the defense the biggest area of growth and said it keeps improving despite losing some critical players. He said the line responded to last week's loss, opening and ending the game with a sack, and he praised the depth and variety of the defensive line room.
Because the defense is playing well, Campbell said the offense can become a chameleon and play whatever way each opponent calls for.
The Lions turn straight to a Thursday Thanksgiving game, with Detroit playing the first game of the day, and Campbell said he is excited about the stakes.

title: Matt LaFleur on Micah Parsons: 'He is an elite player, he is an elite athlete'
headline: Josh Jacobs is a long shot for the Wednesday Thanksgiving-eve game vs. the Rams unless he shows major progress in practice; Micah Parsons is expected back and ramping up.
summary: LaFleur was not optimistic about RB Josh Jacobs for Wednesday's game against the Rams. Jacobs only did individual work and must show a lot of progress in Sunday and Monday practices to be available. LaFleur says the compressed Thanksgiving-eve schedule isn't something he thinks about, and that the team is focused on preparation. He defended Matthew Golden's drop issues, calling him a next-play-mentality player with elite hands who works harder than anyone on the jugs machine. Micah Parsons is ramping up: his rep count is increasing, he was in pads Sunday, and LaFleur anticipates him playing if he clears the remaining hurdles. LaFleur declined to give a snap plan, saying he'd rather not reveal it before the game, and warned that Parsons hasn't played in a long time, so some plays won't look like his usual self. Kevin Zeitler is making progress, and Aaron Banks is working at a couple of positions on the line. LaFleur praised the Rams' deep defensive line (Aaron Donald, Kobe Turner, Braden Fiske and others) and said their two backs show no drop-off between them. He noted that nearly everyone practicing could partly come from the longer layoff since the last game.

injuries.detail: Only did individual work. LaFleur said he must show a lot of progress in Sunday and Monday practices to be available Wednesday, and he is not optimistic.

Rep count in practice is increasing and he was in pads Sunday, the next milestone. LaFleur anticipates him playing if he clears the hurdles but gave no snap count and said he hasn't played football in a long time.
Asked how he looked on the line, LaFleur said only that they're making progress.
Practicing at a couple of positions on the line this week; LaFleur gave no injury or role detail.

signals.claim: Jacobs will not be available Wednesday unless he shows a lot of progress in Sunday and Monday practices.
signals.note: Treat Jacobs as doubtful-leaning for the Wednesday game and line up a backup RB option.
signals.quote: he did some individual, but he's going to have to show a lot of progress

signals.claim: Golden's drops are not expected to cost him his role; LaFleur believes he will work through them.
signals.note: LaFleur is backing Golden publicly despite the drops, so the coach isn't signaling a reduced role.
signals.quote: Every day he catches more balls than probably anybody in this building.

topics.detail: Parsons' practice reps are increasing and he was in pads Sunday. LaFleur anticipates he plays if cleared, but declined to share a snap plan and cautioned that some plays won't look like peak Parsons.
LaFleur said he puts zero thought into the unusual schedule and just maps preparation back from kickoff. Nearly everyone practicing Saturday may partly reflect the longer layoff since the last game.

He called Aaron Donald a nightmare with an elite get-off and said the line is among the deepest in the league (Kobe Turner, Braden Fiske, Tyler Davis, Byron Young). He credited line coach Giff Smith for the stunts and Chris Shula for the scheme.
He said there is absolutely zero drop-off between the Rams' two productive running backs, and he sees similarities between them.
Kevin Zeitler is making progress, and Aaron Banks is practicing at a bit of both of his positions this week.

title: Andy Reid: 'Love Seeing These Young Guys Stepping Up and Making Plays' | Postgame Press Conference - NFL Week 11
headline: Emmett Johnson is carrying a growing pass-game role (catching, blitz pickup, screens) with 100+ yards in the win, and Kansas City turns to Buffalo on a short Thanksgiving week with Noah Gray (ribs) and Ben VanSumeren (knee) hurt.
summary: Reid praised the win over Arizona and singled out young players who are growing quickly. He highlighted Drue Tranquill's eight tackles, George Karlaftis III's two and a half sacks, and Nohl Williams' play at corner. On offense he noted Patrick Mahomes' big day, Emmett Johnson topping 100 yards, and Xavier Worthy's long touchdown, where he called him the fastest man in the NFL. He said Johnson has shown he can catch and block, has picked up blitzes, and is being asked to do many things in the pass game, including screens. Two injuries came out of the game: Noah Gray took a hit to the ribs and Ben VanSumeren tweaked his knee, and Reid offered no detail beyond waiting to see how they respond. Reid said Arizona played a lot of shell coverage and gave up zones, so Kansas City attacked the middle of the field and found the small windows. He credited veteran leadership in the locker room for keeping a young team focused on a short week. The team practices Monday to prepare for Buffalo on Thanksgiving. Reid also praised Karlaftis' relentless, all-business approach.

injuries.detail: Hit in the ribs during the game; Reid said they will see how he does.
Tweaked his knee; no further update, with a short week ahead.

signals.claim: Will keep a significant role in the passing game (receiving, screens) alongside his rushing work.
signals.note: Johnson topped 100 yards and is trusted in protection and as a receiver, which points to a high-floor, three-down role.
signals.quote: We're asking him to do a lot of different stuff in the pass game.

signals.note: Scored a long touchdown that showed off his speed, a reminder of his big-play ceiling.
signals.quote: He was the fastest man in the NFL on that play.

signals.claim: Will keep being a disruptive pass rusher after his two and a half sacks.
signals.note: Reid described his motor and developing pass-rush moves, which is good for IDP managers.
signals.quote: He's smart, tough, all those things.

signals.note: Eight tackles; he is a steady tackle producer for IDP leagues.
signals.quote: ended up having eight tackles.

signals.note: Reid highlighted his improving corner play, which is relevant mostly for IDP.
signals.quote: playing real good football right now

signals.note: Reid said Mahomes knows how to hit the small windows in zone coverage, which suits the middle-of-the-field plan.

topics.detail: Arizona played a lot of shell coverage and gave up zones, with the occasional five-man rush. Kansas City found the small windows in the middle of the field, helped by Travis Kelce and Mahomes.
Reid said the young players are improving by stacking games and learning from mistakes. Veteran leaders keep the locker room from slipping on a short week.
The team practices Monday after a short turnaround and plays Buffalo on Thanksgiving.
Reid declined to expand on a one-two punch at running back, but he praised the quality of backs he has had over his career.

title: HC Jeff Hafley - Nov 22 | Postgame Press Conference
headline: Dolphins lost 26-9 to Buffalo; Kyle McCord struggled under pressure in his second NFL start, Caleb Douglas dropped several passes, and the thin defensive front leans on Chop Robinson and backup Zayne Anderson.
summary: Hafley praised Buffalo but said Miami's missed chances decided the game: drops, a busted coverage on a touchdown, and a 2-of-14 mark on third down. The defense was on the field for 78 plays, and Miami lost the time of possession battle 37 minutes to 23. He was proud of how the team fought, since it was within striking distance with about ten minutes left. Injuries forced new defensive tackles into the lineup, and he credited Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper, who had played little, along with other recently elevated players. Zayne Anderson filled in for Dante Trader, started slowly with a coverage miscommunication on a touchdown, then finished with a sack and an interception. Chop Robinson was praised for playing more big end and six-technique, and Hafley said he is establishing himself as a really good player. Hafley defended Kyle McCord, rejecting McCord's claim that he was responsible for the offense's red-zone failures and pointing to protection, route precision and timing. He was noncommittal on Caleb Douglas's drops and on the pass protection against Greg Rousseau, saying he needs to watch the tape.

injuries.detail: Out for this game, which is why Zayne Anderson got the call-up. The coach did not give any return timeline.

signals.claim: McCord remains the starting quarterback, and the coach has no issues with him despite the offensive struggles.
signals.note: The coach publicly backed McCord and blamed protection and route running, so his job looks safe even though the offense was inefficient.
Douglas had several drops but is still a featured young receiver. The coach would not say whether they were concentration lapses and said it could have been another huge day for him.
signals.quote: it could have been another huge day for him.

signals.claim: Anderson will keep playing while Dante Trader is out.
signals.note: Anderson had a sack and an interception, which makes him an IDP option while he fills in for Trader.
signals.quote: So it's his time again.

signals.claim: Robinson will keep playing more big end and some six-technique because of the injuries on the defensive line.
signals.note: He is playing a lot of snaps, creating pressure and is growing into a bigger role, which helps his IDP value.
signals.quote: I think chop is establishing himself as a really, really good player in this league.

signals.claim: Grant will continue to play a bigger role on the defensive line while the injuries persist.
signals.note: Grant and Keith Cooper were thrust into larger workloads, and the run defense held Buffalo to about 3.5 yards per carry.
signals.quote: Keith Cooper and KG hadn't played very much.

signals.note: Rodriguez followed up a one-tackle game with a strong one that included an interception and a bunch of tackles, a good sign for IDP value.
signals.quote: Jacob had a really good game today.

signals.claim: Pass protection needs to be fixed, and the coach will review whether Jackson needs more help.
signals.note: Protection issues against a strong edge rusher put pressure on McCord and the passing game.
signals.quote: there was times when the protection it wasn't good enough

topics.detail: Miami was 2-of-14 on third down and failed to finish drives in the red zone. Hafley said the team must score touchdowns there and be more consistent.
Miami pressured Josh Allen, sacked him, and intercepted him twice, and held Buffalo to field goals. The defense wore down after 78 plays. A busted coverage and a fake punt were sources of mistakes.
Several recently elevated players were pressed into duty because of injuries. Hafley said the kicker also stepped in and made his field goals, and he liked the kick return.

title: Kellen Moore recaps loss to Chicago | Saints-Bears Postgame | 2026 NFL Week 11
headline: TE Juwan Johnson left with a hamstring injury and the Saints offense stalled again in a 13-point loss to the Bears. Travis Etienne had a 46-yard run, while Jordyn Tyson's snap gap was due to substitution sequencing, not punishment.
summary: Kellen Moore said the Saints had their chances but could not score enough, finishing with 13 points. The only injury he named was Juwan Johnson's hamstring; Johnson did not finish the game and the team will gather more information. Moore blamed fundamentals for the ongoing fumble problem and also pointed to his own receiver substitution communication, which cost timeouts. He said Tyler Shough was hit for a safety because the right tackle did not get a chip from the receiver, Jordyn Tyson, who ran his route without chipping first. He said Shough's interception came as the scramble drill broke down, and he praised Shough for battling. Tyson's roughly 12 snaps off were due to personnel sequencing and tempo, not a punishment or a pitch count. William Sherman went back to center, with Cesar Ruiz able to play either spot and Mason Murphy playing outside. Moore said Etienne's 46-yard run came from winning the edge, and that the early game plan skewed toward passing because of hash marks and attack direction. Moore admitted the offense is not starting fast, stalling in plus territory on opening drives.

injuries.detail: Hamstring injury, did not finish the game. The team will gather more information.

signals.claim: Johnson's hamstring injury will be evaluated further and his availability is uncertain.
signals.note: A TE who left with a hamstring injury is a risk for next week, so check the injury report.
signals.quote: just Jawan had the hamstring. He didn't finish.

signals.claim: Tyson's stretch of about 12 missed snaps came from personnel sequencing and tempo, not a punishment or workload limit.
signals.note: His usage dip does not look like a role change, but the missed chip block that led to the safety is a mistake to monitor.
signals.quote: Just the sequencing of those personnel groups.

signals.claim: Etienne was lightly used early because of a pass-first game plan and then got more work as the game went on.
signals.note: He had a 46-yard run, and the early quiet stretch was attributed to game plan, not a role issue.
signals.quote: we probably didn't have as many run opportunities those first two drives.

signals.claim: Sherman started at center to give the interior line veteran experience.
signals.note: Moore praised him, and the line is shuffling with Erik McCoy, Asim Richards and Taliese Fuaga all listed out, which affects the offense's protection.
signals.quote: Will's a good player.

signals.claim: Ruiz can play either center or guard as the line is rearranged.
signals.note: His flexibility helps the Saints cope with the line injuries.
signals.quote: Caesar can play either spot.

signals.claim: Murphy played on the outside of the line in this game.
signals.note: Moore's praise may mean Murphy keeps a starting role while tackles are injured.
signals.quote: I thought Mason battled on the outside.

signals.claim: Moore expects the offense to fix mistakes, such as scramble-drill discipline and protection help, around Shough.
signals.note: The QB had an interception and a safety, and Moore supports him while saying 13 points is not enough.
signals.quote: I think he battled.

signals.claim: Estime's inactive status will be evaluated week to week.
signals.note: A healthy-scratch RB behind Kamara and Etienne has little fantasy value now.
signals.quote: We'll take that evaluation week to week.

topics.detail: Moore said the Saints' league-leading fumble problem is about fundamentals of protecting the ball. Their lost fumble came on a catch-tuck, and they also had an interception.
The offense is scoring 0.9 points per game in the first quarter. Moore said opening drives are not three-and-outs but stall once they reach plus territory.

Moore took responsibility for unclear receiver substitution communication, which cost timeouts and left the Saints short on them late in the game. Some of the personnel substitutions were predetermined.
Moore briefly considered a field goal on the second final drive but needed a touchdown and a two-point conversion in an 11-point game, so he went for it.
Moore said the right tackle should have had help from a chipper and the edge rusher got there quickly, giving Shough too little time.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: November 22, 2026
headline: DeVonta Smith is back and the offense leaned on him late; Joe Milton III got a strong vote of confidence after the 19-16 win over the Steelers.
summary: Sirianni was pleased to end the seven-game losing streak and said he never doubted the team's effort or preparation. He credited the bye-week self-scout for helping the offense. The team found some explosive plays and solid outside-zone runs, but the production faded later in the game and a few negative plays stalled drives. He said Smith's return mattered, noting the staff "zeroed in" on him to start the second half and that Smith made the key third-down catch late. He praised Joe Milton III for his response and composure, especially on the third-and-six throw to Smith in the four-minute drill. He was upbeat about the defense, saying the front won with block destruction, which let the linebackers Jeremiah Trotter Jr. and Jihaad Campbell make plays. He also noted the defense managed without Zach and after a trade involving Jordan. Riq Woolen left briefly, with Jonathan Jones filling in, then returned and held up on a deep ball. Sirianni said he will need Woolen going forward. He spoke very highly of the opposing quarterback's quick release and of the Steelers overall.

injuries.detail: Back in the lineup after the hamstring issue (full practice on the injury report). Sirianni said it was "good to have him back" and that he is one of the best.
Was taken out during the game, Jonathan Jones covered, then Woolen came back in and was in phase on a deep ball. No injury details given.
Sirianni was asked about playing "without Zach" on defense, which most likely means Baun, but he gave no injury details.

signals.claim: Smith is the featured target in crunch time and the offense will design plays around him.
signals.note: With Smith healthy and the offense scheming touches for him, he should see a high target share, especially in late-game and key third-down situations.
signals.quote: just kind of zero in on some things for him.

signals.claim: Milton keeps the confidence of the staff after executing the key third-and-six throw to Smith in the four-minute drill.
signals.note: Sirianni's praise suggests Milton keeps the offense for now, which helps the passing game's outlook, especially Smith's.
signals.quote: He's confident and, and he should be he's a talented guy.

signals.claim: Woolen will remain a significant part of the cornerback rotation going forward.
signals.note: This is a modest IDP and defensive-matchup signal; he left briefly but returned and was trusted on a deep ball.
signals.quote: I got a lot of faith in him

signals.claim: Trotter was a major playmaker, helped by the defensive front.
signals.note: He is a productive IDP linebacker when the line wins at the point of attack.
signals.quote: running around and making plays

signals.claim: Campbell was a major playmaker, helped by the defensive front.
signals.note: He is a productive IDP linebacker when the line wins at the point of attack.

signals.claim: Smith recorded a sack in the win.
signals.note: A pass-rush contributor for IDP leagues.

signals.claim: Greenard recorded a sack in the win.
signals.note: A pass-rush contributor for IDP leagues.

topics.detail: The coaches used the bye to find what was working and drop the rest. Sirianni saw some explosive plays and effective outside-zone runs, especially early, but said they faded later and a few negative plays stalled drives.
Sirianni was aggressive on third-and-six late and chose to pass instead of run. He said Smith caught the throw and the team wanted the ball in its own hands at the end.
The offense got in and out of the huddle quicker. Sirianni credited the coaches' communication with the players and a good game flow. He said Sean and the staff planned heavily around T.J. Watt.

The defense played well without Zach and after the Jordan trade. Sirianni credited the front for block destruction and the way the game was called. He also said the Steelers' quarterback gets the ball out quicker than anyone he has seen.
Asked about two personal fouls, Sirianni said players should be competitive through the whistle but stop there. He said he was glad the team did not respond further and still backed each other up.

title: WATCH: McCarthy on the loss to the Eagles
headline: Steelers fall to 6-4 after a second straight loss; McCarthy vows to get the ball to the backs more, and Alex Highsmith's ankle has no diagnosis yet.
summary: McCarthy opened by addressing an unnamed player who was ejected after a reported eye-poke on a defender, and who also drew penalties earlier. The coach said the team needs that player and that ejections are unacceptable, but he held off on any punishment until all the information is in. He blamed the slow offense on the run game, where linebackers sitting behind double teams went unanswered. The no-huddle series in the second quarter standardized the defensive calls, and he said Aaron Rodgers managed it well. He took responsibility for not getting the ball to the running backs and promised adjustments. On the five sacks and low yards per attempt, he only said the offense needs to step back and review the up-front matchups. He praised a player he called "Max" (name unclear in the captions) for earning the return-man job and showing trust and route running in his first opportunity. He said the team still has great confidence in its systems at 6-4. He closed by praising Alex Highsmith's energy and professionalism but gave no diagnosis on his ankle.

injuries.detail: Appears to have hurt his ankle; McCarthy said he had no diagnosis yet and would wait to see what the evaluation shows.

signals.claim: Highsmith's ankle injury is not yet diagnosed, so his availability is uncertain.
signals.note: Highsmith's ankle status is unresolved on a short week, so his IDP availability is uncertain until a diagnosis comes.
signals.quote: I don't really have a diagnosis for you on the ankle.

signals.claim: The offense will make adjustments after five sacks and a low yards-per-attempt game, with the up-front matchups under review.
signals.note: Pass protection problems and a stagnant offense put Rodgers' efficiency in question until the adjustments show up.
signals.quote: I thought Aaron managed that.

topics.detail: McCarthy did not name the ejected player in the captions. He called ejections unacceptable, said the team needs him, and said discipline would wait until all the information is in. Five receivers were active.
McCarthy said linebackers played behind the double teams and the offense didn't react quickly enough. He took responsibility for not getting the ball to the backs and said adjustments are coming.
The offense took five sacks. McCarthy credited the opponent's pressure to the up-front matchups and said the team would review them.

A player the captions call 'Max' was elevated and named return man after a healthy camp. He was praised for handling kickoffs and for his route running. McCarthy also mentioned that Kaden Wetjen had been getting plenty of opportunities and that someone named 'Lu' has come on strong. The roster doesn't make the identity of 'Max' clear.
This is the first back-to-back loss. The Steelers are 6-4 and McCarthy expressed great confidence in the team's systems, saying he will own the failure and have a plan by Friday.

title: Todd Bowles on Outcome in Detroit | Press Conference
headline: Ted Hurst III scored twice and Bowles says there's an emphasis on getting him involved earlier, while Baker Mayfield's foot didn't bother him in the loss at Detroit.
summary: Bowles said the Bucs lost to a Lions team that did what it does best better than Tampa Bay did what it does best. He said the Bucs also shot themselves in the foot with mistakes, and that they are 'out of mulligans' and have to win every game from here. He said the run game started slowly because defenses are geared up to stop it early, then opened up as the game went on, and he praised the offensive line. He said there is an emphasis on involving Ted Hurst III earlier in games. He called Hurst's game solid but said the drops must stop, and that Hurst is developing and gets better the more he touches the ball. Bowles said the defense contained Jahmyr Gibbs for three quarters, then missed tackles and took bad angles in the fourth. Mayfield's foot did not affect him, though Bowles still wanted to see how he felt later. The injury updates were that Jacob Parrish has a back issue, Benjamin Morrison has a hamstring issue and Elijah Roberts is in head-injury testing, with no timetable for any of them. Bowles explained the fourth-and-one at the ten-yard line by saying Tampa Bay couldn't win by kicking field goals against that offense. He also said the team lost its composure on the last play and needs to fix that.

injuries.detail: Dealing with a back issue and there is no update. The reporter said 'Jacob Harris', and Parrish is the only Jacob on the roster.
Dealing with a hamstring injury and there is still no update.
Dealing with a head injury, and the team is getting a 'test run' on it.
He was questionable with a foot injury. Bowles said it didn't affect him in the game, but the team will see how he feels later.

signals.claim: Hurst will be more involved earlier in games going forward.
signals.note: He scored two touchdowns and the staff is emphasizing earlier involvement, though drops are still a concern.
signals.quote: There is an emphasis getting more involved in the game.

signals.claim: Mayfield's foot did not limit him in the game, though the team will check how he feels afterward.
signals.note: He moved around well on the foot, but his recovery should be checked on the injury report this week.
signals.quote: Didn't affect him at all.

topics.detail: The run game started slowly because defenses are geared up to stop it early. It loosened up as the game went on, and Bowles praised the offensive line and a running back he called 'Zach', who can't be matched to the roster.
Tampa Bay contained Jahmyr Gibbs for three quarters. In the fourth, missed tackles and bad angles let him make people miss and gain extra yards.
The Bucs went for it on fourth-and-one at the ten-yard line because they didn't think they could beat Detroit's high-powered offense by kicking field goals.

Bowles said the team keeps shooting itself in the foot. He said things got rough on both sides after the last play and the team must control its composure better. He added that they have no margin for error from here on.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Titans' defense gave up 40+ for a third straight game and Saleh offered no fixes. Dan Moore's knee will be evaluated Sunday, and Cam Ward drew mild criticism for end-of-half game management.
summary: Saleh opened the postgame session with injury updates: one player (the name was cut off in the captions) woke up feeling unwell and was held out, Terrell Burgess has a stinger in his knee, and Dan Moore has a knee issue to be evaluated tomorrow. Most of the press conference was about the defense after a third straight game allowing more than 40 points. He called the performance disgusting and embarrassing, and said the problem starts with him. He would not blame scheme or a thinned-out lineup. He said it comes down to winning one-on-one matchups and that Dak Prescott and his receivers played an outstanding game. He felt the offense moved the ball well but settled for early field goals, missed a chance for a touchdown at the end of the first half, and lost the ball in the red zone. He singled out Cam Ward's end-of-half sequence, saying he needs to throw it away or get out of bounds so the team isn't burning clock. Saleh said he will study the tape and that the defense is "stuck in mud" while the offense and special teams have been improving. He did not announce any changes to play-calling or personnel.

injuries.detail: A player woke up not feeling well and was held out of the game; the transcript begins mid-sentence, so the name is missing.
Saleh said he has a knee stinger. No timeline was given.
Knee issue that will be evaluated Sunday. No status was given.

signals.claim: Dan Moore's knee will be evaluated Sunday, and his availability will be clearer after that.
signals.note: An injury to a starting offensive lineman could affect pass protection for Cam Ward and the run game.
signals.quote: Dan Moore had a knee that, uh, we'll all get evaluated tomorrow.

signals.note: Saleh publicly pointed to Ward's end-of-half decision-making as a mistake, but he did not suggest any change to Ward's role.
signals.quote: Cam needs to either ditch it or make sure he gets out of bounds.

topics.detail: The Titans have allowed 40+ points in three straight games. Saleh took responsibility, said he is always going to look inward at how it is being called, and said he would not blame one thing over another.

Saleh felt the offense moved the ball well but stalled in the red zone and on third down. The team settled for early field goals, failed to score at the end of the first half, and turned the ball over in the red zone.
Dak Prescott and the Cowboys' receivers won their one-on-one matchups all game.
